u01l01.objective: I can build and explain a number up to the ten thousands.
u01l01.situation: A cooperative counts 24,638 selected seeds. How can they be counted easily?
u01l01.discover: In a number, each place is worth ten times the place to its right. In 24,638, the 2 sits in the ten thousands place and is worth 20,000, the 4 sits in the thousands place and is worth 4,000, the 6 sits in the hundreds place and is worth 600.

manipulate.title: Build the number 24,638
manipulate.instruction: Build 24,638 by setting the ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and units counters.
manipulate.hint: Start with the ten thousands: how many groups of 10,000 are needed?
manipulate.strongHint: 24,638 is 2 TTh, 4 Th, 6 H, 3 T and 8 U. Adjust each counter one at a time.

example.medium: Intermediate. What number is made of 4 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 9 hundreds, 1 ten and 6 units?
example.reflection: Reflection. In 90,305, what is the value of the digit 3?

practice.title: Break down 40,916
practice.instruction: Build 40,916 by setting the five counters, just like in the guided example.
practice.hint: Look at each digit of 40,916: ten thousands, then thousands, hundreds, tens and units.
practice.strongHint: 40,916 is 4 TTh, 0 Th, 9 H, 1 T and 6 U.

reflect.title: Which number is it?
reflect.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown, then write it in digits.
reflect.hint: Add the ten thousands first, then the thousands, then the rest.
reflect.strongHint: 2 ten thousands make 20,000, 7 thousands make 7,000, 5 tens make 50 and 3 units make 3: 20,000 + 7,000 + 50 + 3.
reflect.prompt: What number is made of 2 ten thousands, 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 3 units?

play.title: Deliver each digit to its place
play.instruction: Deliver the ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and units of 78,402 to the right depot by building the number.
play.hint: Place the ten thousands first, then the thousands, then the rest.
play.strongHint: 78,402 is 7 TTh, 8 Th, 4 H, 0 T and 2 U.

u01l01.remember: Each place is worth ten times the place to its right: ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, units.

check.title: What is the highlighted digit worth?
check.instruction: Choose the exact value of the thousands digit in 63,020.
check.hint: This digit sits in the thousands place: it isn't just worth itself.
check.strongHint: In 63,020, the 3 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 3,000.
check.prompt: In 63,020, what is the value of the digit 3?

u01l02.objective: I can move from words to digits for numbers up to 100,000.
u01l02.situation: A sign at the big market reads "sixty-three thousand and twenty" bags of flour. How can this be written in digits?
u01l02.discover: We spot the thousands first, then the hundreds, tens and units. An empty place is always written with 0: sixty-three thousand and twenty is written 63,020, because there are no hundreds.

manipulate.title: Listen and build
manipulate.instruction: Build each number you are given, using the five counters: 40,005, then 76,000, then 99,999.
manipulate.hint: An empty place is written with 0: don't set that counter if there is nothing at that place.
manipulate.strongHint: 40,005 = 4 TTh, 0 Th, 0 H, 0 T, 5 U. Check each number place by place.

example.easy: Easy. Write in digits: forty-five thousand two hundred and ten.
example.reflection: Reflection. Write the number made of 8 thousands and 7 hundreds.

practice.title: Words and digits
practice.instruction: Match each number to its correct word form, or each word form to its number.
practice.hint: Spot the thousands first, in the words or in the digits.
practice.strongHint: Forty-five thousand two hundred and ten = 45 thousands, then 2 hundreds and 1 ten, so 45,210.

reflect.title: Find the number
reflect.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown, then write it in digits.
reflect.hint: 8 thousands and 7 hundreds: there is no ten, so 0 tens.
reflect.prompt: Write the number made of 8 thousands and 7 hundreds.

play.title: Match the number card
play.instruction: Match each word form to its number card, or each number card to its word form.
play.hint: Count the thousands in the word form before choosing.
play.strongHint: Read the number place by place: thousands, then hundreds, tens and units.

u01l02.remember: We spot the thousands first, then the hundreds, tens and units; an empty place is always written with 0.

check.title: Build the announced number
check.hint: 40,005: how many ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and units?
check.strongHint: 40,005 is 4 TTh, 0 Th, 0 H, 0 T and 5 U.

u01l03.objective: I can compare and order numbers up to 100,000.
u01l03.situation: Two cooperatives show 47,350 and 47,530 bags of maize. Which one has more?
u01l03.discover: We compare the ten thousands first, then the thousands, then the hundreds, the tens and finally the units, place by place from the left.

manipulate.title: Build, then compare
manipulate.instruction: Build 47,350, then 47,530, and look at the first place where they differ.
manipulate.hint: The ten thousands and thousands are the same: look at the hundreds.
manipulate.strongHint: 47,350 has 3 hundreds, 47,530 has 5 hundreds: so 47,530 is bigger.

example.reflection: Reflection. Find two numbers between 9,995 and 10,005.

practice.title: Compare the numbers
practice.instruction: Choose the symbol that correctly compares each pair of numbers.
practice.hint: Compare the ten thousands and thousands of each number first.
practice.strongHint: If the thousands are equal, compare the hundreds, then the tens, then the units.

reflect.title: Order the numbers
reflect.instruction: Place the four numbers from smallest to largest.
reflect.hint: Start by spotting the smallest ten thousands digit.
reflect.strongHint: 18,520 has 1 ten thousand, the other three have 8: compare their thousands and hundreds next.

play.title: Build the biggest reserve
play.instruction: In each round, choose the bigger of the two numbers shown.
play.hint: Look at the ten thousands and thousands of each number first.
play.strongHint: Compare place by place, starting from the left, to find the bigger number.

u01l03.remember: We compare numbers place by place, starting from the ten thousands: as soon as a place differs, it gives the answer.

check.title: Find a hidden number
check.instruction: Write a whole number that is strictly between the two limits.
check.hint: 9,995 and 10,005 don't count: look for a number in between.
check.strongHint: Between 9,995 and 10,005, you can choose for example 9,996, 10,000 or 10,004.

u01l04.objective: I can estimate a result and round a number to the requested place.
u01l04.situation: Along the market road, the markers show 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, then one marker is missing.
u01l04.discover: A pattern moves forward following a regular step. To round a number, we choose the requested place (ten, hundred, thousand or ten thousand) and look at the digit right after it to know whether to round up or stay.

manipulate.title: Continue the pattern
manipulate.instruction: Continue the pattern counting up by 5,000 using road markers.
manipulate.hint: Look at how much the pattern moves forward each time.
manipulate.strongHint: The pattern moves forward by 5,000 each time: 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, then 30,000.

example.medium: Intermediate. Round 24,638 to the nearest hundred.
example.reflection: Reflection. Round 24,638 to the nearest thousand.

practice.title: Complete the pattern
practice.instruction: Find the missing number in the pattern.
practice.hint: Look at the gap between the numbers you already know.
practice.strongHint: The pattern moves forward by 500 each time: after 3,500 comes 4,000.

reflect.title: Round to the nearest thousand
reflect.instruction: Choose the thousand closest to the given number.
reflect.hint: Look at the hundreds digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?
reflect.strongHint: 24,638 is closer to 25,000 than to 24,000, because 638 is closer to 1,000 than to 0.

play.title: Reach the closest marker
play.instruction: Choose the ten thousand closest to the given number on the number line.
play.hint: Look at the thousands digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?

u01l04.remember: To round a number, I look at the requested place and the digit right after it: if it is 5 or more, the place goes up by one, otherwise it stays the same.

check.title: Round to the nearest hundred
check.instruction: Choose the hundred closest to the given number.
check.hint: Look at the tens digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?

u01eval.intro: Work on your own first. Use a drawing if you need to, and explain at least one answer.

q1.title: Question 1
q1.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown.
q1.hint: Add the ten thousands, the thousands, then the rest.
q1.strongHint: 3 ten thousands make 30,000, 5 thousands make 5,000, 2 tens make 20 and 7 units make 7: 30,000 + 5,000 + 20 + 7.
q1.prompt: What number is made of 3 ten thousands, 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens and 7 units?

q2.title: Question 2
q2.instruction: Choose the word form that matches the number shown exactly.
q2.hint: Spot the thousands first: forty-five thousand.
q2.strongHint: 45,210 = forty-five thousand two hundred and ten.

q3.title: Question 3
q3.instruction: Place the four numbers from smallest to largest.
q3.hint: Compare the ten thousands and thousands of each number first.
q3.strongHint: 18,520 has 1 ten thousand, the other three have 8: compare their thousands and hundreds next.

q4.title: Question 4
q4.instruction: Choose the thousand closest to the given number.
q4.hint: Look at the hundreds digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?
